thread.title: County cleans conservation lands - NewsBreak

author: Staff Writer
title: County cleans conservation lands - NewsBreak
text: MONROE COUNTY — The Monroe County Land Authority Land Steward and the Monroe County Sheriff’s Office recently teamed up to conduct cleanups across several protected hardwood hammock conservation properties in the Florida Keys. The collaborative effort addressed issues ranging from illegal dumping to abandoned homeless encampments in conservation areas. By removing debris and restoring the native landscape, the teams are striving to help to protect ecologically sensitive lands that play an important role in the health of the Florida Keys ecosystem. “Conservation lands are community treasures, and it’s important that they’re maintained for ecological protection. We cannot thank the sheriff’s office enough for their participation in helping us with these efforts,” Assistant Monroe County Land Steward Lawrence Lopez said. “The work isn’t easy in the heat, humidity and mosquitoes, but it’s worth it to see these natural areas brought back to a cleaner, safer state.” The land authority continues to acquire and manage properties that preserve critical habitats, protect water quality and reduce development pressure in environmentally sensitive areas. The land steward regularly monitors these lands to ensure they remain healthy. Additional joint cleanups will be done as new sites are identified.
